update description: Needs identification becomes an upfront, digital-first, and cross-program responsibility. The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is expected to proactively scan for data reuse, contribute to cost and timeliness analyses, rigorously document the rationale for new collections, and use digital tools to assess the feasibility and sustainability of meeting statistical needs before escalation to new projects.
interdependencies: 4.1 - Frame and source data selection activities may increasingly depend on documented data reuse scans and feasibility assessments produced at needs identification
2.1 - Design activities will rely on standardized rationale, operational feasibility, and automation-readiness documentation generated upfront
8.1 - Evaluation and audit functions will depend on traceable, standardized records of decision rationale and client needs assessment
impact reasoning: This update shifts the role from primarily responding to user requests and coordinating downstream retrieval/validation/dissemination activities toward an earlier-stage diagnostic and gatekeeping function. The incumbent will be expected to determine whether existing internal or external data assets can satisfy needs before new collection or major system change is pursued. This requires structured and evidence-based client engagement, use of digital inventories and metadata-driven discovery tools, and explicit assessment of operational feasibility, timeliness, sustainability, and automation-readiness. As a result, the role expands from interpreting requests and implementing improvements to systematically documenting business rationale, constraints, reuse options, and handoff-ready records that support auditability and downstream design work.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This activity will broaden to include pre-operational diagnostic work before retrieval and dissemination begin. Coordination will increasingly start with determining whether an identified need can be met through reuse of existing data assets, whether digital processes are available, and whether the request is operationally feasible and sustainable. The activity becomes less purely execution-focused and more intake-, triage-, and assessment-oriented.

update description: Stakeholder needs consultation shifts from primarily person-to-person liaison and exploratory interpretation toward an evidence-based, digitally enabled consultation workflow using machine-actionable metadata and data discovery platforms. The Coordinator must first assess whether client needs can be met from existing assets, document decisions and trade-offs transparently, and only advance new tabulation or collection proposals when unmet needs are clearly demonstrated and justified through cost-benefit and burden considerations.
impact reasoning: This update changes the role from a mainly consultative and request-translation function into a more structured gateway role for assessing need feasibility through digital discovery, metadata interrogation, and documented decision workflows. The Coordinator will still engage clients and subject matter specialists, but the first response to requests will increasingly be platform-enabled assessment of existing data assets, their fitness for purpose, reusability, and constraints. Ad-hoc requests will be screened more systematically against available holdings, agency priorities, cost, respondent burden, and operational feasibility. The role therefore becomes more accountable for transparent triage, rapid evidence-based recommendation making, and formal documentation of rationale. This also implies more frequent adjustment to changing standards, platforms, and feedback cycles, increasing the expectation for operational agility and continuous process realignment.

update description: Needs assessment and service response cycles become shorter and more iterative, with more frequent process feedback, documentation, and realignment. The Coordinator must support rapid digital consultation cycles while maintaining transparency, consistency, and alignment with organizational priorities.
impact reasoning: This update increases the speed and cadence of the role. The Coordinator will be expected to move quickly from request intake to evidence-based assessment while preserving quality and traceability. The role will need to operate within tighter turnaround expectations, adapt to ongoing process refinements, and maintain consistency across repeated review cycles. This introduces a stronger requirement for agility, disciplined documentation, and comfort working within evolving digital operating models rather than stable, manually mediated consultation patterns.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Participates as a subject area representative on various teams and working groups.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Participation will involve more frequent feedback loops on consultation processes, metadata usability, and service triage practices, not only subject-matter representation.

gaps.justification: The role will need to contribute to ongoing process refinement cycles that are not explicit in the current activity.
gaps.name: Continuous improvement participation
gaps.description: Ability to provide structured feedback on workflow effectiveness, identify bottlenecks in digital consultation processes, and contribute to iterative service improvements.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement program activities.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Leading work groups will increasingly require managing shorter planning horizons, reprioritizing based on intake evidence, and reinforcing adaptation to revised procedures and standards.

gaps.justification: Shorter cycles and more frequent realignment create a need for stronger adaptive leadership than the current wording implies.
gaps.name: Short-cycle operational planning
gaps.description: Ability to organize and reprioritize work under compressed timelines and evolving process requirements while maintaining service quality.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Operational management becomes more dynamic, requiring rapid reallocation of effort in response to intake outcomes, platform changes, or revised guidance from management.

gaps.name: Adaptive workload management
gaps.description: Ability to shift resources and sequence work in response to fast-moving consultation outcomes, revised priorities, and iterative management feedback.

gaps.name: Training on digital consultation tools and practices
gaps.description: Ability to train colleagues and users on metadata platforms, discovery workflows, decision documentation, and client communication standards.

gaps.description: Knowledge of how changes in intake, metadata discovery, and triage processes affect downstream production, coordination, and service delivery systems.

update description: Shift from manual, expert-driven concept identification and user-needs interpretation to metadata-driven, AI-assisted concept discovery, enterprise standards alignment, and machine-actionable outputs. The role evolves toward validating, prioritizing, and arbitrating system-suggested concepts rather than generating concepts from scratch.
interdependencies: 2.1 - Specify Needs: user requirements capture becomes more structured and machine-readable to support automated concept identification
2.3 - Establish Output Objectives: concept harmonization and machine-actionable metadata influence output design and dissemination structures
4.3 - Classify and code: standardized concepts and metadata alignment affect downstream coding and classification consistency
5.2 - Integrate data: interoperability and enterprise metadata alignment support integration across sources
7.1 - Update output systems: machine-actionable concept definitions and metadata must be maintained in dissemination environments
impact reasoning: The work-description will change by reducing the relative emphasis on individually creating or informally refining concepts, definitions, and user-request interpretations through manual expert judgment alone. Instead, the position will increasingly work through enterprise metadata repositories and AI-assisted recommendation tools that surface candidate concepts, definitions, linkages, and standards. The EC-03 will still apply subject-matter expertise, but more as a validator, arbitrator, and harmonizer of system-generated suggestions. Operationally, this means requests for custom tabulations, retrieval, validation, and dissemination will begin with structured discovery of existing enterprise concepts and metadata assets before new concepts are proposed. The role will also need to ensure that selected concepts are interoperable, aligned with enterprise standards, and suitable for downstream machine use. Responsibilities will therefore expand to include evaluating AI-generated recommendations, resolving conflicts between local program requirements and enterprise standards, and documenting concept decisions in reusable, standardized formats. This also suggests future role evolution toward stewardship of concept quality, metadata coherence, and system-supported decision-making rather than predominantly manual subject-matter development.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - "Provides custom tabulations and time-series information for ad-hoc client requests."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Ad-hoc requests will increasingly require the use of enterprise metadata and AI-assisted concept discovery tools to identify already-defined concepts, comparable variables, and harmonized data structures before producing customized outputs. The activity shifts from interpreting requests primarily through personal expertise toward translating requests into structured, standards-aligned concept searches and validating the relevance of system-suggested options.

gaps.justification: The current activity emphasizes fulfilling ad-hoc requests but does not explicitly require use of metadata repositories, AI-assisted discovery, or standards-based concept matching. Future performance depends on the ability to work with these tools and assess their outputs.
gaps.name: Metadata-enabled requirements interpretation
gaps.description: Ability to convert client requests into structured concept, variable, and metadata queries using enterprise repositories and standardized metadata models.

gaps.justification: System-suggested concepts will need to be reviewed for appropriateness before outputs are produced; this exceeds the current manual interpretation focus.
gaps.name: AI-assisted concept validation
gaps.description: Ability to evaluate, confirm, reject, or refine AI-recommended concepts, variables, and definitions based on program relevance and statistical coherence.

gaps.justification: The update explicitly requires alignment with enterprise standards and interoperability, which is not fully reflected in the current ad-hoc service orientation.
gaps.name: Enterprise metadata standards and interoperability principles
gaps.description: Knowledge of enterprise concept registries, metadata standards, common models, and interoperability principles used to align requests and outputs across programs.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - "Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Improvements to methods and procedures will increasingly include integrating metadata-driven concept identification, standards harmonization, and AI-supported recommendation logic into operational workflows. Changes to systems and applications will need to support machine-actionable concept definitions and reusable metadata assets rather than only local program-specific process adjustments.

gaps.justification: The current wording supports procedural improvement but does not explicitly require designing workflow changes around metadata-driven and AI-assisted concept management.
gaps.name: Metadata-integrated process design
gaps.description: Ability to redesign operational and processing workflows so that concept identification, validation, and documentation are embedded in metadata-driven systems.

gaps.justification: Future systems work depends on understanding how AI recommendations are produced and how they should be governed in production settings.
gaps.name: AI recommendation logic and limitations
gaps.description: Knowledge of how AI-assisted recommendation tools generate concept suggestions, including strengths, limitations, bias risks, and validation requirements.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - "Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Subject-matter advice will increasingly involve guiding users through enterprise-standard concepts, explaining AI-assisted matches or recommendations, and resolving cases where automated suggestions do not align cleanly with business needs. Advice becomes less about creating bespoke concepts and more about steering users toward harmonized and reusable conceptual assets.

gaps.justification: The advisory role now requires communicating the rationale behind standards-aligned, system-suggested concepts rather than only explaining program-specific concepts.
gaps.name: Standards-based advisory communication
gaps.description: Ability to explain enterprise-standard concepts, metadata structures, and AI-assisted recommendation outcomes to users in clear operational terms.

gaps.justification: The role evolution emphasizes arbitration and conflict resolution between system outputs and program needs, which extends beyond current advisory expectations.
gaps.name: Concept arbitration and harmonization
gaps.description: Ability to resolve conflicts among user needs, local program concepts, and enterprise-standard or AI-suggested concepts while preserving coherence and usability.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - "Identifies and assesses trends and developments in the subject area; reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content and determines the implications for statistical methods and procedures."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Decision-making will expand beyond subject-matter trends to include evaluating changes in enterprise metadata standards, concept registries, and AI-enabled discovery capabilities. The position will need to determine not only methodological implications, but also whether existing concepts can be reused, harmonized, or require escalation for gap resolution.

gaps.justification: The current decision-making focus is on subject-area developments; future decisions must also account for metadata ecosystem changes and AI-enabled concept discovery methods.
gaps.name: Enterprise data holdings and concept landscape
gaps.description: Knowledge of available enterprise datasets, concept inventories, metadata assets, and their relationships to support reuse and harmonization decisions.

gaps.justification: The update requires adjudicating among system-suggested concepts and identifying conceptual conflicts or gaps.
gaps.name: Concept gap and conflict assessment
gaps.description: Ability to identify when AI-suggested or enterprise-standard concepts do not sufficiently meet program needs and to determine appropriate escalation or remediation.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - "Develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This element will shift from direct creation of concepts and definitions toward validation, selection, refinement, and controlled extension of system-discovered concepts. New concept development will become more exceptional and will likely occur only after enterprise assets and AI-suggested options have been reviewed and found insufficient.

gaps.justification: The current element centers on creating methods and concepts; future work requires knowing when not to create new concepts and how to manage reuse-first workflows.
gaps.name: Reuse-first concept stewardship
gaps.description: Ability to prioritize reuse, extension, and alignment of existing enterprise concepts before proposing new definitions or methods.

gaps.justification: Machine-actionable outputs are explicitly required in the future state, while the current element does not mention structured metadata expression.
gaps.name: Machine-actionable metadata representation
gaps.description: Knowledge of how concepts, definitions, and relationships must be documented in structured forms that support automation, discovery, and downstream system use.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - "Identifies and evaluates problems related to the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Problem identification will increasingly include detecting failures or weaknesses in AI-assisted concept matching, metadata quality, standards alignment, and interoperability across systems. Recommendations to management will need to address governance and quality issues in automated concept processes, not only traditional operational issues.

gaps.justification: Current problem-solving language is broad, but future problems are specifically rooted in metadata quality and AI-supported concept identification processes.
gaps.name: Metadata quality assessment
gaps.description: Ability to assess completeness, consistency, usability, and standards alignment of metadata used in concept discovery and dissemination processes.

gaps.justification: AI-enabled operations create new technical and conceptual failure modes not explicitly covered in the current role description.
gaps.name: Governance risks in AI-assisted concept processes
gaps.description: Knowledge of governance, traceability, explainability, and quality assurance requirements for automated or AI-assisted concept identification workflows.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 3. Communication - "Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, and to establish project plans and target dates."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Liaison activities will require translating user requirements into metadata specifications, concept mappings, and structured business rules that can be consumed by AI-assisted or metadata-driven systems. Collaboration will increasingly include enterprise data stewards, metadata specialists, and platform teams rather than only program subject-matter specialists.

gaps.justification: The current liaison role does not explicitly require expressing requirements in metadata-ready or machine-consumable forms.
gaps.name: Machine-readable requirements specification
gaps.description: Ability to express business and subject-matter requirements as structured metadata, mappings, and rules suitable for automation and system integration.

gaps.justification: The role now depends on engagement with enterprise-wide metadata and platform functions beyond traditional program contacts.
gaps.name: Enterprise metadata governance processes
gaps.description: Knowledge of organizational roles, approval pathways, stewardship models, and governance processes for enterprise concepts and metadata assets.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 3. Communication - "Provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Advice to users will expand to include explaining how metadata-driven systems identify concepts, what confidence or rationale sits behind AI-assisted recommendations, and when human arbitration is required. User support will therefore become more interpretive of system outputs and enterprise standards.

gaps.justification: The future role requires the incumbent to help users understand AI/metadata-assisted processes and limitations, which is not explicit in the current advisory requirement.
gaps.name: Explainability-oriented user support
gaps.description: Ability to explain automated concept recommendations, their evidentiary basis, limitations, and implications for users' data requests and outputs.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - "Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify subject-matter concept and definition requirements, and to conduct studies."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Program-area knowledge remains important, but future performance requires combining domain knowledge with awareness of enterprise concepts, metadata assets, and standardized definitions. Identification of concept requirements will be less purely domain-derived and more mediated through enterprise discovery and harmonization mechanisms.

gaps.justification: The current knowledge requirement is domain-centric; the update adds a need to connect domain issues to enterprise metadata and standardized concepts.
gaps.name: Crosswalk between domain concepts and enterprise standards
gaps.description: Knowledge of how program-specific concepts relate to common enterprise definitions, classifications, and metadata structures.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 4. affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This knowledge area must now include metadata-driven retrieval, semantic discovery, standards-based concept alignment, and AI-assisted support for concept and output selection. Advising on subject-matter development becomes advising on how concept choices work across enterprise systems and dissemination channels.

gaps.justification: The current knowledge statement focuses on conventional retrieval/editing/validation/dissemination methods, but the update introduces metadata and AI-enabled methods.
gaps.name: Semantic and metadata-driven data discovery
gaps.description: Knowledge of metadata-based search, semantic relationships among concepts, and standards-supported retrieval approaches used to identify appropriate data assets.

gaps.justification: The future role explicitly emphasizes FAIR alignment and interoperability, which are not explicitly present in the current knowledge requirements.
gaps.name: FAIR and interoperability principles
gaps.description: Knowledge of findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability principles as applied to concepts, metadata, and statistical data products.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - "Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems; to design specifications for the editing and validation of data, and to maintain and use databases."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: System knowledge will need to extend beyond traditional processing systems to metadata platforms, concept registries, and AI-enabled recommendation services. gaps.justification: Current system knowledge does not explicitly include metadata platforms or AI-enabled components that become central in the future process.

gaps.description: Knowledge of the structure, functions, and integration patterns of metadata repositories, concept registries, and related enterprise platforms.

gaps.justification: Future system design must support concept traceability and machine-actionable outputs, which are not currently foregrounded.

gaps.justification: The current statement is program-network focused, while the future role requires wider enterprise visibility and the ability to evaluate conceptual reuse opportunities.

gaps.justification: Current analytical expectations focus on concepts and definitions in a conventional sense; future analysis must also account for interoperability and machine-actionable consequences.
gaps.name: Interoperability impact analysis

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 6. Research and analysis - "Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Interpreting requests will move from a predominantly manual analysis of user intent to a hybrid process in which requests are decomposed into metadata elements, matched against enterprise concepts, and assessed using AI-assisted recommendation tools. Feasibility assessment will increasingly depend on whether suitable standardized concepts already exist and how well they align with requested outputs.

gaps.justification: This element is directly transformed by the shift from manual interpretation to metadata-driven and AI-assisted matching.
gaps.name: Structured request decomposition
gaps.description: Ability to break user requests into standardized conceptual, definitional, and metadata components that can be evaluated through enterprise systems.

gaps.justification: The role evolution requires the incumbent to arbitrate among system-suggested options rather than simply interpret requests manually.
gaps.name: Recommendation arbitration
gaps.description: Ability to compare and adjudicate among multiple system-suggested concepts or data options based on statistical validity, user needs, and enterprise alignment.
